newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty falls on foreign T-bill sales on shallow mkt.
newsitem.headline: Zloty falls on foreign T-bill sales on shallow mkt.

text.p: The zloty tumbled below the parity rate on Monday as the dollar/mark jump and small foreign T-bill sales moved the very shallow market, dealers said.

They said the zloty, under a cloud from the fall of the Czech crown, Poland's widening current account gap and some calls for maintaining the 1998 budget deficit at this year's level, slid more as a result of lack of demand for it than large foreign sell offers.
"The zloty's fall was caused by a number of reasons which all combined to take it down below the parity rate," said Leszek Szafranek of Bank Slaski.

"The market is very shallow because many banks are not active during holidays, the dollar mark rate surged and foreign players were selling zlotys because of debates over next year's budget gap and the trade deficit outlook," he said.
The zloty closed at 3.3790/30 against the dollar and 1.8860/70 against the mark at 0.77 percent below the parity rate against 0.28/0.15 percent above the rate on Friday.

In late afternoon trade it slid further to 0.90/0.99 percent below the parity rate or 3.880/10 against the dollar and 1.8905/25 against the mark. "I expect it will keep on falling tomorrow," one dealer at a foreign bank here said.

The NBP had no comment on the zloty's fall, but analysts said that the fact the the central bank had not intervened to support the zloty showed it was not concerned with the unit's weakening and considered it "normal market play".

On the money market O/N and T/N offers rose between 0.05 and 0.25 point to 22.70/22.30 and 23.15/23.50 percent as the money market adjusted to rising T-bill and NBP-bill yields, and braced for a potential change in this year's budget.
Poland's parliament will break its summer recess on Wednesday to decide on how to raise cash to help those affected by the floods.
At the primary T-bill tender yields of all papers rose even though total demand was just above the one billion zloty offer with the average benchmark up to 22 percent.
Foreign players stayed on the sidelines at the auction, wary of entering Polish instruments before parliamentary polls in September.
